key_insight: Neural Harmonic Textures attach compact harmonic encodings to primitives (e.g., Gaussians) so each primitive can represent high-frequency appearance, enabling high-quality novel-view synthesis while retaining the scalability of primitive-based reconstructions.
problem_solved: Primitive-based representations (like 3D Gaussian Splatting) are efficient and scalable but lack expressivity per primitive, making it hard to capture fine high-frequency texture and detail.
method: Anchor latent feature vectors to a virtual multi-scale coordinate system around primitives so each primitive gains a localized feature field.
Use harmonic basis / neural decoding to synthesize high-frequency texture detail from those anchored latents, improving expressivity without increasing primitive count.
Integrate the textures into the primitive rendering/composition pipeline to produce higher-fidelity novel views while preserving scalability.
impact: Delivers significantly better visual detail for primitive-based reconstruction pipelines with modest overhead, making high-quality novel-view synthesis more practical for large scenes and production workflows.
